Regulation: B.C. Reg. 135/2026
Made under: Workers Compensation Act
Published in: No. 14 – B.C. Regs. 125 to 148, July 28, 2026
Deposit date: July 20, 2026

B.C. Reg. 135/2026, deposited July 20, 2026, under theWORKERS COMPENSATION ACT[section 110]. Resolution of the Workers’ Compensation Board, dated July 17, 2026. The Workers’ Compensation Board orders that, effective November 6, 2026, the Occupational Health and Safety Regulation, B.C. Reg. 296/97, is amended as set out in the attached Appendix. — W. L. CRONK,Chair, Board of Directors. 1	Section 8.39 of the Occupational Health and Safety Regulation, B.C. Reg. 296/97, is repealed and the following substituted: 8.39(1)	In this section and sections 8.40 and 8.41,"tight-fitting respirator"means a respirator that requires an effective seal with the face for proper functioning. (2)	If a worker is required to wear a tight-fitting respirator, the employer must not permit anything to interfere with the seal or the proper functioning of the respirator. 2	Sections 8.40 (1) and 8.41 (1) are amended by striking out "respirator which requires an effective seal with the face for proper functioning" and substituting "tight-fitting respirator". 3	Section 8.40 (2.1) (a) and (3) is amended by striking out "a respirator" and substituting "a tight-fitting respirator". minutes_briefs.title: BC tight-fitting respirator rules updated: employers must keep seals working from November 6, 2026
minutes_briefs.summary: BC Regulation 135/2026 changes the Occupational Health and Safety Regulation (the workplace safety rules) effective November 6, 2026. It adds a clear definition of a 'tight-fitting respirator' (a mask that needs a good seal against the face to work properly). It also adds a new duty: if a worker must wear one, the employer must not let anything interfere with the seal or how the respirator works. The change also replaces long wording in sections 8.40 and 8.41 with the new short term.
minutes_briefs.action_required: By November 6, 2026, check your workplace rules and gear so nothing (like facial hair, straps, or other equipment) breaks the seal on tight-fitting respirators.

key_dates.label: BC tight-fitting respirator rule takes effect
